title: Universe compatibility of finite-cone categorical-pattern models
statement:
Fix nested Grothendieck universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P=(B,S,\{p_a:K_a^{\triangleleft}\to B\}_{a\in A})$ be a $\mathcal U$-small categorical pattern as in [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], with all $2$-simplices of $B$ included in the scaling. Assume that every $K_a$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices; empty $K_a$ are allowed. Use marked simplicial sets, their markings $K^\flat$ and $K^\sharp$, and monomorphisms from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and the pattern model structures $\mathsf M_P(\mathcal U)$ and $\mathsf M_P(\mathcal U')$ from [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus], formed with the identical fixed pattern $P$.

The following maps form a common $\mathcal U$-small generating set of cofibrations in both model structures: $(\partial\Delta^n)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$, for every $n\geq0$ and simplex $\Delta^n\to B$, and $(\Delta^1)^\flat\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, for every edge of $S$. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of the proper faces of the standard simplex. A generating set $I$ means that the cofibrations are exactly the retracts of transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of maps of $I$, with coproducts and transfinite sequences small in the universe of that model structure. A $\mathcal U$-small marked object is fibrant in one model structure if and only if it is fibrant in the other. A map between $\mathcal U$-small marked objects is a weak equivalence in one model structure if and only if it is a weak equivalence in the other. There are functorial fibrant replacements $X\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{\mathcal U}X$ and $X'\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{\mathcal U'}X'$ and a natural isomorphism $\iota R_{\mathcal U}\cong R_{\mathcal U'}\iota$, compatible with these replacement maps, where $\iota$ is the inclusion of the smaller marked objects into the larger ones. In particular, $R_{\mathcal U}X$ is $\mathcal U$-small for every $\mathcal U$-small $X$.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Definition B.1.1 (seven pattern-anodyne generator types), Proposition B.1.6 (fibrancy), Lemma B.2.4 (homotopy-inverse criterion), and proof of Theorem B.0.20 (small-object fibrant replacement), printed pp.1470-1471,1483,1485-1487. Universe compatibility is the finite-generator small-object consequence expanded in report.md; not a separately numbered theorem. Marked cofibration generators also occur in the proof of Proposition B.1.9, printed p.1476. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: In either universe cofibrations are underlying monomorphisms by [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. Apply the boundary-cell presentation of underlying monomorphisms in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] to $X\hookrightarrow Y$, label each attached simplex by its composite to $B$, and give each attached simplex the flat marking. The pushouts retain exactly the old marked edges; after all underlying simplices have been attached, add the remaining marked edges of $Y$ using $(\Delta^1)^\flat\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$. Each added edge maps into $S$, since $Y\to(B,S)$ preserves markings. This is an $I$-cell presentation; its coproducts and ordinal are small in the universe of $Y$. Conversely each generator is an underlying monomorphism, and this property is preserved by pushouts, transfinite composites and arrow retracts: degreewise these operations adjoin elements without identifying old elements, take unions, and take retracts of injections. Thus retracts of $I$-cell maps are exactly all cofibrations. The index set $\coprod_{n\geq0}B_n\amalg S$ belongs to $\mathcal U$, and the same labelled maps define $I$ in both universes.

source.place: Proposition B.1.9, proof, generating cofibrations, printed p.1476; degreewise marked refinement of the boundary-cell presentation.

proof.text: Use the seven explicit types $J_P$ of [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-generators]. Every domain and codomain has finitely many nondegenerate simplices: this is immediate for simplices, horns and their marking changes; $Q$ is a quotient of the finite simplex $\Delta^3$; and a nondegenerate simplex in a join is in one factor or is the concatenation of a nondegenerate simplex from each factor. The finite $K_a$ therefore make types (B1) and (C2) finite as well, including $K_a=\varnothing$. All labels for these finite shapes are maps into the fixed $\mathcal U$-small $B$, together with $a\in A$ and a natural number. Thus $J_P$ is a common $\mathcal U$-small family in both universes. Its lifting characterization and the fibrant-object characterization of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] give the same fibrancy test in both universes. For a smaller $X$, maps from each domain or codomain to $X$ are literally the same functions with the same face, degeneracy, marking and base conditions. Consequently existence of each extension is unchanged, which proves fibrancy compatibility.

source.place: Definition B.1.1 and Proposition B.1.6, printed pp.1470-1474; finiteness observation at the start of the proof of Theorem B.0.20, printed p.1485.

proof.text:
Here is an explicit replacement construction in either universe. Put $X_0=X$. For each $m\geq0$, form the set $T_m(X)=\{(j,u):j:D_j\to E_j\in J_P,\ u:D_j\to X_m\text{ a marked map over }B\}$. Define $X_{m+1}$ by the pushout
$$X_m\amalg_{\coprod_{(j,u)\in T_m(X)}D_j}\coprod_{(j,u)\in T_m(X)}E_j,$$
where the first attaching map on the summand $(j,u)$ is $u$. Set $RX=\operatorname{colim}_{m<\omega}X_m$. These colimits exist directly: take degreewise coproducts and quotients for pushouts, then degreewise sequential colimits; mark exactly the images of the marked edges. The structure maps to $(B,S)$ descend because the attaching maps are over $B$. Every transition is a pushout of a coproduct of generators, so $X\to RX$ is a countable $J_P$-cell map. Each transition is an underlying injection, including the generator types which change only markings.

source.place: Theorem B.0.20, proof, initial finite-cone small-object construction (a)-(c), printed p.1485; construction expanded degreewise.

proof.text: Any marked $u:D_j\to RX$ factors through some $X_m$: the transitions are underlying injections, so identify $RX$ degreewise with their union. Choose a common stage containing the images of the finitely many nondegenerate simplices of $D_j$. Every simplex is a degeneracy of a nondegenerate simplex: if it is degenerate, write it as a degeneracy of a simplex of lower dimension and repeat; the dimension strictly decreases until this process stops. Applying the resulting degeneracy maps to the chosen images keeps every image in the same subcomplex. Faces, degeneracies and the base equation are reflected by the inclusion $X_m\hookrightarrow RX$, giving a simplicial map over $B$ without additional choices. Increase $m$ to witness the marking of the images of the finitely many marked nondegenerate edges; degenerate edges are already marked at every stage. The copy of $E_j$ indexed by this map at stage $m+1$ extends $u$ into $RX$. The lifting theorem [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-generators] makes $RX$ $P$-fibered, hence fibrant by [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. The same theorem makes the countable $J_P$-cell map $X\to RX$ a trivial cofibration, hence a weak equivalence. This proves that the explicit construction is a fibrant replacement in each universe.

source.place: Proposition B.1.6, Example B.2.2, and proof of Theorem B.0.20 (b)-(c), printed pp.1471-1474,1482,1485; finite-domain extension argument expanded.

proof.text: For a marked map $f:X\to Y$ over $B$, construct $f_m:X_m\to Y_m$ inductively. At a successor stage send the summand labelled $(j,u)$ to the summand labelled $(j,f_m u)$ by the identity of $E_j$, and use the pushout property; at the limit use the induced colimit map. The label formula respects identity maps and compositions, so $R$ is a functor and $\eta:X\to RX$ is natural. If $X$ belongs to $\mathcal U$, every $T_m(X)$ is $\mathcal U$-small (it is a union, indexed by $J_P$, of subsets of function sets between $\mathcal U$-sets). Coproducts, quotients and the countable colimit stay in $\mathcal U$ by its closure axioms. Use these same degreewise set constructions in both universes. Inductively the label sets agree for smaller inputs and the pushout quotients agree, since the equivalence relation generated by the identical attaching identifications is identical. The sequential unions and their markings agree too. These identifications give $\iota R_{\mathcal U}\cong R_{\mathcal U'}\iota$. On each cell they are identities on the $E_j$ coordinate and preserve its label, so they commute with $R(f)$ and with $\eta$. This proves the required naturality and compatibility, as well as smallness of $R_{\mathcal U}X$.

source.place: Theorem B.0.20, proof, finite-cone small-object construction, printed p.1485; explicit functorial and universe-relative expansion of that construction.

proof.text: For a map $f:F\to G$ between fibrant marked objects, the mapping-test characterization in [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] implies that $f$ is a weak equivalence if and only if it has a marked homotopy inverse over $B$, with homotopies parameterized by $(\Delta^1)^\sharp$. Here are both arguments. If $f$ is weak, test first with $Z=F$: surjectivity on $\pi_0$ gives $g:G\to F$ with $gf$ in the component of $1_F$. Test with $Z=G$: injectivity on $\pi_0$, together with $fgf$ in the component of $f$, puts $fg$ in the component of $1_G$. The mapping complexes are Kan. To identify their path components with vertices modulo edge paths, apply [lem-cbc-kan-realization-mapping-classes] with $K=\Delta^0$: continuous maps from a point modulo homotopy are precisely path components, and the displayed bijection is natural in the Kan target. Finite edge paths can be replaced by single edges by filling $2$-horns: for $e:x\to y$, fill $\Lambda_0^2$ with vertices $(x,y,x)$, edge $01=e$ and edge $02=1_x$ to obtain an edge $12:y\to x$; for edges $x\to y\to z$, fill $\Lambda_1^2$ to obtain the edge $02:x\to z$. A path of length zero is represented by the degenerate edge. These edges give the two required marked homotopies. Conversely, for every fibrant $Z$, precomposition with $g$ is a homotopy inverse to precomposition with $f$ on the sharp mapping complexes. Write $H:F\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp\to F$ for the homotopy from $gf$ to $1_F$ and $J:G\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp\to G$ for that from $fg$ to $1_G$. If $a:\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(F,Z)$ corresponds to $\widetilde a:F\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Z$ and $t:\Delta^n\to\Delta^1$, send $(a,t)$ to the map $(x,s)\mapsto\widetilde a(H(x,t(s)),s)$. This is marked and over $B$, commutes with every simplicial operator, and has endpoints $a\circ gf$ and $a$. Replacing $(F,H,a)$ by $(G,J,b)$ gives endpoints $b\circ fg$ and $b$. These formulas are precisely the homotopies between the two composites of precomposition maps and their identities. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to conclude the mapping maps are weak homotopy equivalences, and apply the mapping-test criterion. For smaller $F,G$, all inverse maps and homotopies just described are functions between smaller sets, and the sharp mapping complexes between them have identical simplices in both universes. The criterion is therefore identical in the two universes. The Kan horn-filling assertion used here is [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]; no test against a larger target is inferred merely from tests against smaller ones.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4, (1) iff (2), printed p.1483; the formal two-test inverse argument and its sharp simplicial homotopies written out.

proof.text: Finally let $f:X\to Y$ be any map of smaller marked objects. Naturality gives $R(f)\eta_X=\eta_Y f$. By step 4 both units are weak equivalences in each universe, so two-out-of-three in the model structure of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] says that $f$ is a weak equivalence if and only if $R(f)$ is, separately in each universe. Step 5 identifies the two maps $R(f)$ and keeps their fibrant endpoints smaller; step 6 gives their identical weak-equivalence criterion. Hence $f$ has the same weak-equivalence status in both universes. All clauses of the statement now follow from steps 1, 2, 4 and 5.

source.place: Proof of Theorem B.0.20, reduction from f to E(f), printed p.1485; two-out-of-three applied to the common replacement.

split_report.summary: Preserved every hypothesis and clause. Proved common generating cofibrations, compared fibrancy via the seven explicit pattern-anodyne types, constructed the compatible replacements by countably adjoining all finite lifting problems, and reduced weak-equivalence comparison to an explicit homotopy-inverse test between smaller fibrant objects. One new statement-only node isolates the pattern-anodyne lifting theorem; no Lean attachment or Mathlib match.
split_report.blueprint: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction before R lim: technical pattern models below lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus; the finite-cone replacement and universe comparison in step 5 of lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operadic-tensor-adjunction. Steps 1-7 supply the finite-cone model-size input used in step 5 of the nonsymmetric-operadic tensor adjunction, without changing the integral-adjoint route.

tool_uses.why: Generic simplicial homotopy-inverse implies weak homotopy equivalence, applied only to testing mapping complexes in step 6; this technical model argument does not replace any geometric unit route.

The K=Delta^0 case identifies edge components of the Kan testing complexes with path components of their realizations, to justify extracting marked inverse homotopies in step 6; a generic tool, with no replacement of the unit route.

B.2.2, Lemma B.2.4 and the finite-K proof of B.0.20 (printed pp. 1467-1487). New node lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-generators: all seven generators match B.1.1 term by term once every 2-simplex is scaled. C0's first-edge-in-S condition is forced by the domain's marking. Extension against the generators is the same as extension against their weakly saturated class, which is B.1.6, and triviality of that class is B.2.2/B.1.14; no finiteness is needed. It satisfies B1-B7, is not a duplicate of the marked-anodyne, relative-replacement, saturation or small-direct-colimit nodes, and restates no clause of the item. Steps: (1) boundary-cell presentation plus a marking-only pass, giving a U-small label set. (2) Finite shapes, including K_a empty, so the same extension test in both universes. (3)-(4) Explicit all-attaching-maps countable cell construction: finite domains factor at a stage, so RX is P-fibered and X->RX is a trivial cofibration. (5) Identical set constructions give an actual natural isomorphism compatible with eta. (6) B.2.4 (1)<=>(2) expanded: I checked the horn fills, the precomposition homotopy formula and its endpoints (vu=(fg)^*, uv=(gf)^*), and that only F and G serve as test objects. (7) Two-out-of-three. The two tool_uses (lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak, lem-cbc-kan-realization-mapping-classes) are generic and accepted. The statement is unchanged, nothing is weakened, and there is no SGA use. No fixes made.
